thread:
shilpa: Heads-up — customer `acme-inc` seeing intermittent 403s when hitting /v1/generate on Dedicated. Happening ~1-2% of requests. Attached request IDs from their logs below, can someone help repro?

shilpa: Request IDs: req_20240302_aa12, req_20240302_ab99, req_20240302_ac07. They say curl works sometimes but fails when their service rotates servicekey.

devin: thanks. any chance they can paste the exact curl they use (with headers redacted)? also need the raw Authorization header value (or prefix) and the x-redwood-org / x-redwood-project headers if present.

shilpa: pasted what they sent (redacted):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_SERVICEKEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "x-redwood-org: org-acme" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-4b","input":"hello"}'
```

shilpa: They also included a snippet from their client showing they rotate service key and then retry, sometimes getting 200 then 403 on immediate retry.

luke: devin — based on patterns we've seen, it can be a scope mismatch (servicekey vs org-scoped token) OR header canonicalization during signature verification. Could you try repro with a quick agent that rotates keys quickly + repeated requests?

devin: will try. quick questions: do we have the exact server-side request_id header that matched those failing requests? the logs from our edge usually have X-RW-ReqId (e.g., rw-req-xxxx). if you have those I can trace to the LB and see which signer rejected it.

shilpa: their logs show "x-rw-reqid: rw-5f34e2a" for req_20240302_ab99; they matched it to our response where body was 403 + message "scope_mismatch".

eng-oncall-bot: Trace found: rw-5f34e2a -> upstream node n12 -> verifier=v1.8.6 -> signature_status=invalid_scope. Linked trace: https://traces.redwood.ai/traces/rw-5f34e2a

devin: ok that points to scope check failing on our side. Two likely repro angles: 1) client rotates service key but continues sending old x-redwood-org header (project/org mismatch after rotation) 2) signer canonicalizes headers and order changes cause signature to be computed over different header set. I'll try both.

shilpa: Customer also reported that when they switched to a user token (not servicekey) the failures stopped. so looks like servicekey-scopes indeed.

devin: repro steps I'm running now (will paste exact curl):

```
# 1) obtain servicekey A (scoped to project:acme-prod)
# 2) send request with x-redwood-org: org-acme and x-redwood-project: acme-staging (mismatch)
# 3) rotate to servicekey B (scoped to project:acme-staging) and immediately retry previous request header set

# example curl (simulating rotate):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer SERVICEKEY_A" \
  -H "x-redwood-org: org-acme" \
  -H "x-redwood-project: acme-staging" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-4b","input":"test"}'
```

devin: preliminary: I can reproduce a 403 if the token scope doesn't include the project header value in its allowed scope set. Also saw a case where client lib sent headers in different order and our HMAC verifier tolerated it, so order alone isn't the cause.

luke: good. can we capture a failing request raw headers (as received by our edge) and the signature base-string used to verify? that will let us confirm whether the token->scope map vs header mismatch is the root cause.

shilpa: customer willing to share debug bundle. I've asked them to run: `curl -v` to capture full exchange and paste the redwood response headers and both client request/response. they say they can provide logs and the time window 2024-03-02 17:12-17:18 UTC.

devin: once they upload debug bundle, include the following: 
- the client Authorization header prefix (first 10 chars ok)
- the x-rw-reqid from our response
- the server edge raw headers (from traces link)
- a sample of their rotation timing (how quickly they swap keys)

support-bot: support ticket created: #SUP-21345. Added customer debug bundle placeholder.

shilpa: customer uploaded bundle to the ticket. link: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/SUP-21345/bundle-20240302.zip

devin: grabbing bundle now. I'll extract the request/response pairs and paste the raw base-string used by verifier.

(devin pasted later) devin: extracted: base-string used for signature:
```
POST
/v1/generate
host: api.redwood.ai
content-type: application/json
x-redwood-org: org-acme
x-redwood-project: acme-staging
...body hash ...
```

devin: and the token A scopes: projects:acme-prod, models:read. So token didn't include acme-staging — verifier rejected with scope_mismatch. That matches customer seeing success when switching to user token which had broader scopes.

luke: thanks. root cause: rotation + stale header set: they rotate to a key that doesn't cover the project they immediately continue to send in x-redwood-project. two mitigation suggestions:
- customer: ensure rotation swaps both token and any associated org/project headers atomically or canonicalize to use org-only tokens if needed.
- platform: add clearer error message suggesting which required scope was missing (we already log it but maybe respond with a more actionable code) and add a diagnostic header in 403 pointing to required scope id.

shilpa: customer preferred quick fix on their side. we've documented repro steps and recommended they use a short window drain after rotation. I'll close after customer confirms.

support-bot: Ticket #SUP-21345 updated: status -> awaiting_customer.

shilpa: leaving notes for postmortem: include example curl, the reqid rw-5f34e2a, and the verifier trace link.

luke: sounds good. if customer sees recurrence after changes ping me and we'll consider adding the diagnostic header. :thumbsup:
